original_text: THE SETTLING INTERFACE REQUEST TO crates/ocean asks for PROFILE queries, not point lookups: current, temperature, salinity and pressure on depth levels from surface to local bottom at one horizontal position and time, because the descent integral dt = dz/w walks the column monotonically. Non-negotiables stated in it: geographic east/north m/s (not grid-relative); resolved vertical velocity flagged present/absent rather than returned as zero (a silent zero systematically shortens displacement); the detailed-bathymetry-cell-deeper-than-model-bottom case as a flagged testable condition; a declared uncertainty model for unresolved deep and near-bottom motion; one coherent ocean-error realisation per impact event; and the ability to repeat a run against a different product without code change. Product choice is explicitly left to the shared owner.

original_text: SLOW SINKERS DRIVE THE TIME-AXIS REQUIREMENT ON THE OCEAN PRODUCT: daily means are adequate for a 15-70 minute descent at 1-5 m/s but not for the slow-sinking tail, where an element stays in the water column for many hours, so sub-daily output (or an explicit statement that the axis is daily) matters more to settling than horizontal resolution. Settling's default is to download nothing, not even a small regional test subset, until the shared ocean owner exists.

original_text: The GLORYS12V1 profile column settling uses (glorys12v1_uo_vo_thetao_so_20140307-20140314.profile.json) covers only 80-112°E x 45-18°S. The GLORYS12 surface-current series and ERA5 extend 15-120°E, 50-0°S. So settling's run.toml fields_window/bathymetry_window [80,112,-45,-18] cannot be widened north without a wider column. Impacts north of 18°S are recorded as not computed and excluded: <0.02 % on reference-289; up to 0.035-0.048 % in estimable next-run single-stratum panels; 0.30 % in routes-H1. Settling has asked ocean transport for the same product over 75-115°E x 45-10°S. Windowed loads are bit-identical, so widening changes no in-window result.

original_text: The repository holds no sea-state, wind-for-detection, cloud-cover or daylight fields for the 2014 search and imaging dates. These covariates set the detection probability for every surface term: the aerial and ship search, other satellite sightings, imagery-coverage non-detections, AIS ship transits and Pléiades. They must be built together with the surface-search term, or those terms fall back to a constant detection probability.
